traits.leaf_area_per_basal_area.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 74 birches (Betula pendula and B. nigra): 0.311 m² of leaf a cm². Median leaf area over trunk area at breast height of its open-grown street and park trees 20 cm or more through, the trees the broadleaf median (0.167) was taken over.

traits.crown_spread.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 48 birches 25 years or older (Betula pendula and B. nigra): 0.59. Median crown width over height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees.

traits.crown_see_through.note: Sky inside the crown outline of six side views of leafy open-grown birches against clear sky (2026-10-25, plantgen-claude project-files/tree-shape/round3-2026-10-25/BIRCH.md; imagekit run measure-skycolour-birch-2026-10-25): sky by colour, the tree cropped by eye, plantc measure-mask. Betula pendula inat:294973161 0.11, inat:331977194 0.29, inat:394508815 0.41, inat:628368217 0.37, inat:717317748 0.22; B. papyrifera inat:82778231 0.30 (half a crown, mirrored). Median 0.30, the genus's as its pendulous, thin crowns read in Sargent ('narrow open head'). Lower crowns that stood against forest were cut off, which may raise it.

traits.crown_base_share.note: USDA Urban Tree Database (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, RDS-2016-0005), TS3 raw tree data: its 48 birches 25 years or older (Betula pendula and B. nigra): 0.17 (quartiles 0.13 and 0.22). Median height of the crown's base over the tree's height of its trees 25 years or older (15 or older where it has fewer than 10 that old), measured open-grown street and park trees, which are often pruned up for clearance.

appearance.bark_look.thickness.note: The genus's bark thickness as its reference species', betula-papyrifera (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/betula-papyrifera.json): text: FOFEM 0.027; base of old trunks to 1/2 in (Sargent)

appearance.bark_look.stages.twig.note: The genus's twig stage as its reference species, betula-papyrifera, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/betula-papyrifera.json): stage: text: twigs dark orange to dull red to 'dark orange-brown, lustrous', 'orange-colored oblong lenticels' (Sargent)

appearance.bark_look.stages.young.note: The genus's young stage as its reference species, betula-papyrifera, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/betula-papyrifera.json): stage: text: 'young trunks and branches dark reddish brown, smooth ... lenticels pale, horizontal' (FNA); until_diameter_m: inferred (photo): white at ~3 y (Wikipedia) or 10-12 y (Silvics)

appearance.bark_look.stages.white.note: The genus's white stage as its reference species, betula-papyrifera, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/betula-papyrifera.json): exfoliation: text: 'readily exfoliating in paper-thin sheets' (FNA); 'fine horizontal strips' (Wikipedia); inner 'pale orange color when first exposed' (Sargent); sizes inferred; lenticels: text: 'in maturity dark, much expanded, horizontal' (FNA); 'long narrow ... raised' (Sargent); sizes inferred; until_diameter_m: inferred (photo)

appearance.bark_look.stages.black base.note: The genus's black base stage as its reference species, betula-papyrifera, shows it (plantgen-claude project-files/bark/records/betula-papyrifera.json): stage: text: 'on old trunks for a few feet above the ground ... dull brown or nearly black, sharply and irregularly furrowed and broken on the surface into thick closely appressed scales' (Sargent)

traits.terminal_bud.note: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, analytical key to the genera, pp. xxiii-xxiv): 'Terminal buds wanting; branchlets prolonged by an upper axillary bud' leads, with Carpinus and Ostrya, to Betula (p. 205).

traits.short_shoots.note: Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson 1978, pp. 59-60: Acer, Betula, Corylus, Fagus and rosaceous fruit trees such as Pyrus have a well-developed short-shoot system, whose short shoots fill most of the crown and bear most of its leaves (Wilson's red maple).
